notes: Single source of truth for Acme usage guidance and the 7 error categories. The linter rules, the Sonnet judge prompt, and the Gemini Decision 1 questions are all derived from this file. Change categories here and nowhere else.
principles: Use Acme components before building custom UI. If a component exists for the job, use it.
Style only with tokens. Never use raw color values, and never use spacing values outside the scale.
Pick tokens by meaning, not by look. A token that happens to be the right color is still wrong if its purpose is different.
Destructive styling is reserved for irreversible or data-losing actions.
Brand color is for brand expression, never for status, errors, or actions.

rules.rule: Colors must come from tokens (CSS variables or the TS token map). No hex, rgb(), hsl(), or named colors.
padding, margin, gap, and inset values must use space.* tokens. Raw px values are allowed only if they are on the spacing scale, and tokens are still preferred.
color.text.secondary is only for text on color.surface.default. On tinted, subtle, or colored surfaces, use color.text.primary.
Error and failure states use color.feedback.error.*. Success uses color.feedback.success.*; warnings use color.feedback.warning.*.
color.brand.* is for brand moments only (hero highlights, logo lockups, marketing callouts). Never use it for errors, status, validation, or action buttons.
Interactive controls use color.action.* tokens. Don't reuse action tokens for static decoration.

guidance.primary: The single most important action in a view. At most one primary Button per view or dialog.
guidance.secondary: Supporting actions next to a primary action, such as Cancel or Back.
guidance.destructive: Irreversible or data-losing actions: delete, remove permanently, revoke access. Pair it with a confirmation.
guidance.ghost: Low-emphasis actions in dense UI, such as toolbars and inline edits.

dont: Don't use primary for destructive actions, even when they're the main action in a dialog.
Don't use destructive for reversible actions like Archive or Sign out.
Don't put two primary Buttons in one view.

Alert.guidance: Inline, persistent messages about the state of a page or form. Danger is for errors and failures.
dont: Don't restyle an Alert with brand or action tokens.
Don't build alert-like boxes from Surface plus custom colors; use Alert.

Chip.guidance: Compact, removable or selectable items: filters, tags, multi-select values.
dont: Don't hand-build pill-shaped divs or spans for tags or filters; use Chip.

Badge.guidance: Static, read-only labels such as counts and status labels. Not interactive.
dont: Don't use Badge for removable or clickable items; use Chip.

Input.guidance: Single-line text entry. Always has a visible label. Errors go through the error prop, which uses color.feedback.error.*.
dont: Don't render a raw <input> with custom styles.

Surface.guidance: Container for grouped content. Replaces Card.

Card.guidance: Deprecated in 0.1.0. Use Surface. Card will be removed in 1.0.

Stack.guidance: Layout spacing between children. Prefer Stack gap over margins on children.

categories.name: Hardcoded value
categories.question: Does this file use a raw color value (hex, rgb, hsl, or named color) instead of an Acme token?

categories.name: Off-scale spacing
categories.question: Does this file use a padding, margin, gap, or inset value that is not on the Acme spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px)?

categories.name: Deprecated component
categories.question: Does this file import or render a deprecated Acme component, such as Card?

categories.name: Contrast failure
categories.question: Does this file put a text token on a surface where it fails the contrast rules, such as color.text.secondary on a tinted or colored surface?

categories.name: Semantic misuse
categories.question: Does this file use a token whose meaning doesn't match its purpose, such as a brand or action token on an error, status, or validation message?
categories.example: An error message colored with color.brand.primary

categories.name: Wrong variant
categories.question: Does this file use an Acme component with a variant or intent that contradicts its guidance, such as a primary Button for an irreversible delete?

categories.name: Wrong component
categories.question: Does this file hand-build UI that an existing Acme component already provides, or use a component meant for a different job?
categories.example: A pill-shaped <span> with an x button instead of <Chip onRemove>
